findings.title: Release gate silently drops a coordinate finding that is not in the report's Dependencies list (fail-open)
findings.description: decide() does `continue` for any finding whose dependency is a group:name:version coordinate absent from the '## Dependencies' section ('not shipped: test scope or compileOnly'). The scan is already limited to runtimeClasspath (release.gradle scanConfigurations), so the skip adds no correctness, but it opens a hole: ReleaseMain.findingsFromCsv takes the FIRST pkg:maven purl of the Identifiers cell, so a High/Critical row whose first purl is a related or version-normalised coordinate that is not byte-equal to the resolved graph entry is dropped instead of blocking. A completed report whose Dependencies section is empty (hand-edited or truncated graph) also passes every coordinate finding. The gate is the release block, so it must fail closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not skip unknown coordinates: block them (unless excepted) like jar-name findings, or at minimum fail the gate when a completed report has an empty Dependencies section. Keep the test-scope case (fr_REL_003_AC4) by excluding such artifacts at scan time, not by ignoring findings at gate time.

findings.title: An existing but empty or header-less Dependency-Check CSV is recorded as 'completed, no findings'
findings.description: scan-report only checks csv.isFile(); findingsFromCsv returns an empty list when parseCsv yields no rows, and ScanReport.fromChild(exit==0, empty list) then writes 'Status: completed ... no findings'. A zero-byte or truncated report file with child exit 0 therefore passes the release gate as cleared. A report with the expected header but missing the CVE/Identifiers columns is likewise treated as zero findings. The only pending trigger is a missing file or a non-zero exit.
findings.suggested_fix: In findingsFromCsv/scan-report return null (so fromChild writes pending TOOL_ERROR) when there is no header row or the header lacks the 'CVE' and 'Identifiers' columns; add a ScanReportTest case with an empty file and a header-less file.

findings.title: A lower-version numeric score wins over a higher-version severity band
findings.description: The score loop (v3, v4, v2) runs completely before the severity-band loop. A row with CVSSv3_BaseSeverity=HIGH/CRITICAL but an empty v3 score and a CVSSv2_Score of 5.0 gets cvss=5.0 (Medium) and the band is never consulted, so the finding does not block. The test csvRowsWithoutScoreOrPurlKeepTheirSeverityAndJarName only covers rows with no score at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve per version in order v3, v4, v2: use the score, else that version's severity band, and only then fall to the next version; add a test row with v3 severity HIGH, v3 score empty and v2 score 5.0.

findings.title: Contradictory dead branch in ops_REL_004_AC1: the 'verified' check can never be reached
findings.description: The test first handles `if ("verified".equals(java8[1]))` (requiring a recorded 'run java8' line) and then unconditionally asserts `assertEquals("pending", java8[1])`. Whenever the first branch is entered the second assertion fails, so the branch is dead and the doc test pins 'pending' forever, contradicting matrixRules which accepts a verified Java 8 row with a run link. The first branch gives a false impression that a recorded Java 8 run is supported.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the verified branch and keep the pending pin with a comment that a Java 8 run changes this test, or assert pending-or-(verified with a recorded java8 run) consistently.

findings.title: Text guard for 'no release task wired into the default build' misses common forms (assemble, tasks.check, nested braces)
findings.description: wiresReleaseTaskIntoDefaultBuild only recognises tasks.named('check|build|test') blocks and `check|build|test.dependsOn/finalizedBy` calls. release.gradle itself documents that the CycloneDX plugin hangs its task on `assemble` (which `build` runs), but `assemble` is not a guarded target; `tasks.check { }`, `tasks.getByName('build')`, `tasks.matching {}` and a block containing a nested closure (`[^}]*` stops at the first brace) are not caught either. The 'offline default build must not break' invariant is therefore only weakly defended; no test executes a default `build -m` with the release property absent and asserts that no release task is in the plan.
findings.suggested_fix: Add assemble/tasks.check/getByName to the target pattern, and add a TestKit dry run (`build -m` without -Prelease) asserting no task name matches RELEASE_TASK.

findings.title: project.hasProperty('release') enables the release script for any value or any gradle.properties entry
findings.description: `-Prelease=false`, or a `release=` line in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties or gradle.properties, makes hasProperty true and applies gradle/release.gradle, whose buildscript resolves two plugins from the plugin portal. A default offline build on a machine that happens to define such a property would break, which is the invariant CON-BUILD-017 protects. GUARDED_APPLY in ReleaseScriptTextTest pins this exact text, so it also locks the weaker form in.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard with `project.findProperty('release') == 'true' || project.hasProperty('release') && project.property('release') == ''` (or document that only -Prelease is supported) and adjust GUARDED_APPLY accordingly.

findings.title: License deny regex over-matches 'CDDL + GPLv2 with classpath exception' style names and any 'Commercial' substring
findings.description: DENIED matches the substring GPL anywhere, so a single-license entry such as 'CDDL + GPLv2 with classpath exception' (the exact name ThirdPartyLicensesTest uses for javax.servlet) fails the shipped check although the classpath exception makes it permissible, and 'Non-Commercial'/'Commercial use permitted' wording matches 'Commercial'. These fail closed, but the only escape is a hard-coded override list in release.gradle that is limited to TinyHttpd today.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document that such licenses must be added to the override list, or special-case 'classpath exception' / dual 'CDDL' names; add a LicenseCheckTest case stating the intended verdict for 'CDDL + GPLv2 with classpath exception'.

findings.title: sdsAc11 makes the default build depend on the git binary, .git history and a pinned wave-7 commit
findings.description: `git diff --stat f7da71d -- spi` and `git status --porcelain` run inside the default `./gradlew build` test. From a source archive without .git, a shallow clone lacking f7da71d, or any later wave that legitimately touches spi, the test fails with an unrelated git error (assertEquals(out, 0, p.waitFor())). It also fails whenever a developer has an uncommitted edit under spi, regardless of intent.
findings.suggested_fix: assumeTrue the .git directory and the commit exist (git cat-file -e f7da71d), and pin the spi surface by a content hash or file listing instead of a git ref.
